scores.rationale: Empty {} is the actual OTLP success reply from a real collector, so it passes though it carries no values. Fully accepted export with an empty span in the request; nothing contradicts it.

errorMessage is a natural developer-facing warning with rejectedSpans "0", a pattern the OTLP spec permits. It accurately refers to the request's empty attribute value and empty span, and full acceptance matches rejectedSpans 0.
partialSuccess with errorMessage "" and rejectedSpans "0" is valid, though a real server would normally omit empty defaults. Zero rejections with an empty message is a consistent full success.
errorMessage "" and rejectedSpans "0" is valid OTLP, though real servers usually omit defaults. Zero rejected with no message is consistent full acceptance of the request.
rejectedSpans "0" with empty errorMessage is a valid reply, slightly unusual since defaults are normally omitted. Consistent full-success semantics for the request.
partialSuccess with only rejectedSpans "0" is plausible, though a real server would likely omit it. Int64-as-string form is correct, and zero rejections consistently means full acceptance.
